skill.name: hubspot-automation
skill.description: Use Rube MCP to automate HubSpot CRM workflows for contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and custom properties.
skill.summary: Guide HubSpot CRM operations through Rube MCP with safe setup, search, batching, and property workflow guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code for MCP and HubSpot tool names. The only confirmed static issue is the documented external Rube MCP endpoint, an intended low-severity network dependency that requires user trust and OAuth approval. No prompt injection, hidden command execution, or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown inline code triggered command-execution scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify in metadata or documentation that these are MCP tool slugs and parameter names, not executable shell commands.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on an external Rube MCP endpoint for HubSpot workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Document the third-party data path, OAuth scopes, and user approval requirements before users connect HubSpot.

remediation.issue: CRM search guidance can be confused with system reconnaissance by generic scanners.
remediation.suggestion: State that search steps are limited to HubSpot CRM records and are used only for duplicate prevention and filtering.

content.value_statement: HubSpot teams lose time creating records, checking duplicates, and handling pipeline details. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe Rube MCP workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup of the Rube MCP endpoint and HubSpot OAuth connection.
Provides tool sequences for contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and custom properties.
Explains HubSpot search filters, internal property names, and pagination cursors.
Documents batch operation limits and chunking guidance for 100-record batches.
Maps common HubSpot tool slugs to their key parameters.
Highlights auth, date, duplicate, and response-structure pitfalls.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active HubSpot connection before workflows can run.
Does not provide HubSpot credentials or bypass OAuth approval.
Does not execute workflows unless the AI client can call MCP tools.
HubSpot permissions, rate limits, and schema rules still apply.

use_cases.title: Create Clean Contact Records
use_cases.description: Search for existing contacts, validate fields, and create new records only when duplicates are not found.

use_cases.title: Track Deal Pipeline Activity
use_cases.description: Find deals by pipeline, stage, owner, or date while resolving HubSpot IDs into readable labels.

use_cases.title: Manage Support Ticket Searches
use_cases.description: Search tickets with exact internal property names, selected fields, and cursor-based pagination.

prompt_templates.title: Create One Contact
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a single CRM contact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the HubSpot automation skill to create one contact. Verify the Rube HubSpot connection, search by email, and ask for missing fields before creation.

prompt_templates.title: Find Deals in a Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Search HubSpot deals in the named pipeline. Retrieve pipeline stages first, filter by stage and owner, and summarize the matching deals.

prompt_templates.title: Import Companies in Batches
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for bulk CRM updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a HubSpot company import. Confirm property names, chunk records into batches of 100, create companies, and report errors separately.

prompt_templates.title: Design Custom Properties
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for CRM schema changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan HubSpot custom properties for the specified object. Check existing properties and groups, define enumeration values, and warn about immutable property names.

output_examples.input: Create a contact for a new lead after checking for duplicates.
output_examples.output: Connection verified. No duplicate contact was found. The contact was created and the returned HubSpot ID was recorded for follow-up.

output_examples.input: Find open deals in the enterprise pipeline owned by a named representative.
output_examples.output: The pipeline and owner IDs were resolved. Matching open deals were listed with stage labels, amounts, close dates, and pagination status.

output_examples.input: Create a dropdown property for ticket priority categories.
output_examples.output: Existing ticket properties and groups were checked. The property plan included internal name, label, field type, options, and creation warnings.

best_practices: Call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before workflows so current tool schemas are used.
Search existing CRM records before create operations to reduce duplicate records.
Use internal HubSpot property names and paginate until no next cursor remains.
anti_patterns: Do not create contacts or companies without a duplicate search.
Do not use display labels when HubSpot requires internal property names.
Do not batch more than 100 records in one HubSpot request.

faq.question: Does this skill require a HubSpot account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an active HubSpot connection through Rube MCP before CRM tools can be used.

faq.question: Can it create contacts and companies?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents single and batch workflows for contacts and companies, including duplicate checks.

faq.question: Can it manage deal pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides deal searches, pipeline lookup, stage lookup, and owner resolution.

faq.question: Does it support custom HubSpot properties?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to list properties, choose groups, and create or update property definitions.

faq.question: Does it avoid duplicate CRM records?
faq.answer: It recommends searching existing contacts or companies before creating new records.

faq.question: Is Rube MCP a required external service?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill depends on the Rube MCP endpoint and the Composio HubSpot toolkit.
